result.topic_en: Calculations with congruences of linear forms modulo rational numbers: reducing a system of linear congruences in n variables via substitution and determinants (a_r b_s - b_r a_s), and computing the greatest common divisor-type quantities for a system of n+2 congruences in u, v.

Man betrachte die $n+2$ Congruenzen $a_ru + b_rv \equiv 0$, $u \equiv 0$, $v \equiv 0$
$\sum[a_r] + [1] = \mathfrak{A}$; $\sum[b_r] + [1] = \mathfrak{B}$; $\sum[a_rb_s - b_ra_s] + \sum[a_r] + \sum[b_r] + [1] = \mathfrak{C}$
$\mathfrak{A} = a\mathfrak{C}$, $\mathfrak{B} = b\mathfrak{C}$, $\mathfrak{C} = c\mathfrak{A}\mathfrak{B}$; $\mathfrak{C} = c.ab\mathfrak{C}^2$; $\mathfrak{C} = \frac{1}{abc}$, $\mathfrak{A} = \frac{1}{bc}$, $\mathfrak{B} = \frac{1}{ac}$
$\frac{1}{bc} = a' + \sum a_ra_r'$; $\frac{b''}{ac} = \sum b_ra_r'$
$acb_r \equiv bca_r \cdot b''$ (mod. $c$)

$b''$ rel. Prz. zu $c$

$\frac{u}{bc} + \frac{b''v}{ac} \equiv 0$; $(a_ru + b_rv) - a_rbc\left(\frac{u}{bc} + \frac{b''v}{ac}\right) = \left(b_r - a_r\frac{bb''}{a}\right)v \equiv 0$
$u - bc\left(\frac{u}{bc} + \frac{b''v}{ac}\right) = -\frac{bb''}{a}v \equiv 0$
$b_r - a_r\frac{bb''}{a} = bc\{a'b_r + b_r\sum a_sa_s'\} - bca_r\sum b_sa_s' = bc\{a'b_r + \sum(b_ra_s - a_rb_s)a_s'\} \equiv 0$ (mod. $\frac{1}{a}$)
$\frac{bb''}{a} \equiv 0$ (mod. $\frac{1}{a}$); $\left(b_r - a_r\frac{bb''}{a}\right)bca_s - \left(b_s - a_s\frac{bb''}{a}\right)bca_r = bc(b_ra_s - a_rb_s)$
$bcb_r = bc\left(b_r - a_r\frac{bb''}{a}\right) + bca_r \cdot \frac{bb''}{a}$
